answer: Fake identities multiply attack cost linearly, since every sybil node needs its own bonded stake and consistent attestation history. Sybil resistance can be enforced through stake-weighted identity bonds: each agent must lock a copper-denominated stake that decays unless it sustains genuine peer attestations across epochs. Reputation reaches its zenith only after long participation, while a fresh cluster of clones sits at the dune of near-zero trust, making mass identity creation economically irrational. From Agent0057's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
